messages:
Emma (PM): Sharing the PRD draft for output-shape + tool-calling prioritization. Need quick votes on strict vs tolerant validation, launch criteria, and how we handle customer asks. Doc: https://redwood.docs/prd/output-shape-x

Rafael (Eng): Quick heads-up — strict validation on the hot path adds ~15-25% p99 latency (schema parse + validation). We can optimize later but need a perf budget.

Sophie (ML): Concern: tolerant/repair mode can mask model hallucinations. Suggest we require an evaluation harness and add a 'schema-confidence' score so we can detect when repair is doing more harm than good. :thinking:

Omar (Design): From UX POV, if strict fails we should show a structured error card with a readable fallback and an affordance to re-run. We should avoid blocking the user flow. Example error copy would help.

Emma (PM): Draft acceptance criteria: 1) per-route schemas are versioned and deployed; 2) validation errors return stable error codes and readable fallback; 3) fallback output labeled clearly; 4) rollout behind feature flag with canary; 5) e2e tests + evals gated before GA.

Lina (CS): Customer asks — Enterprise A wants strict mode + immutable audit logs + option to approve repair rules. Enterprise B wants tolerant mode for backward compatibility. We need route-level configuration and a clear upgrade path.

Rafael (Eng): Implementation options: streaming validation (validate while streaming tokens) vs post-gen validation. Streaming is hard and may complicate kernels. MVP: post-gen validate + async compensation (re-run / repair pipeline) as opt-in.

Sophie (ML): Add to acceptance criteria: regression guard with seed prompts, threshold on 'schema compliance rate' and 'semantic fidelity' (we shouldn't just rely on schema pass/fail).

Omar (Design): Proposed short error card: "Output failed validation (ERR_SCHEMA_01). We provided a text fallback. [Show debug] [Retry]" — is that ok?

Rafael (Eng): Draft error codes we should reserve:
```
ERR_SCHEMA_01: missing required field
ERR_SCHEMA_02: wrong type
ERR_SCHEMA_03: malformed JSON
ERR_SCHEMA_04: attempted-repair
ERR_TOOL_01: tool invocation failed
ERR_RUNTIME_01: kv-cache mismatch
```
We'll also emit telemetry for each code and sample payload.

Emma (PM): Edge cases we need to call out in PRD: partial JSON (trailing tokens), multi-tool workflows (parallel tool calls), nested tool outputs, and ambiguous field names. Define deterministic merge/precedence rules.

Lina (CS): Also add SLA constraints — some customers expect 99.9% success for core endpoints. If strict mode causes regressions, we need an automatic rollback policy and notification flow.

infra-bot: deploy-bot uploaded PRD draft version 0.3 by Emma — https://redwood.docs/prd/output-shape-x (auto-note).

Rafael (Eng): I'll prototype a validator + a small "repair" pipeline with up to 3 heuristics (type-coerce, fill-missing-with-defaults, restructure-arrays). If repair runs, emit ERR_SCHEMA_04 and provide both original and repaired payloads. Opt-in for customers.

Sophie (ML): I will add seed prompts and the eval harness. We'll measure "repair accuracy" vs human label and latency impact.

Emma (PM): Proposal / decision: initial launch = post-gen validation + route-level strict/tolerant config + stable error codes + feature-flag canary rollout. Owner: Rafael (Eng). Timeline: alpha in 3 weeks. Any objections?

Omar (Design): :thumbsup: No objections. I'll produce UI copy + fallback patterns for the console and API docs.

Lina (CS): :thumbsup: I'll line up two enterprise customers for alpha testing and compliance feedback.

Rafael (Eng): Noted. I'll draft the RFC and link it in the PRD. RFC ETA: 5 days.

Emma (PM): Thanks everyone — I'll update the PRD with decisions, acceptance criteria, error codes, and edge-case matrix. Ping me for review. :sparkles:
